practice.heading: Two areas of law, practised properly.

overlap.title: Where they meet
overlap.body: A separation can put your status at risk. A sponsorship can collapse mid-application. Most firms hand you to a second lawyer at exactly that moment — we don't.

process.heading: You will always know what happens next.

steps.title: Talk to us
steps.body: Thirty minutes, free, in the language you prefer. Tell us the situation — we'll tell you honestly whether you need a lawyer at all.

steps.title: A written plan
steps.body: Before any money changes hands you receive the strategy, the timeline, and a flat fee where possible — in both languages.

steps.title: We do the work
steps.body: Filings, correspondence, and hearings handled by us. You get an update at every stage, whether or not there is news.

counsel.name: Nasrin Shirazi
counsel.quote: “I arrived here at nineteen with a file I couldn't read. Nobody should have to argue for their own family in a second language.”
counsel.body: Called to the bar in Ontario, with fifteen years spent almost entirely on immigration and family files for Persian-speaking clients. Appears before the IRB, the Federal Court, and the Ontario Superior Court of Justice.

team.heading: Two more voices in the room.

members.name: Aram Kiani
members.title: Senior Associate — Immigration
members.body: Called to the bar in 2015. Handles Express Entry, provincial nominees, and refusal appeals — with a particular focus on files that have already gone wrong once.

members.name: Leila Farrokhzad
members.title: Associate — Family Law
members.body: Joined the firm in 2021 after five years at a Toronto family law boutique. Handles separations, support claims, and mehrieh recognition.

items.quote: They explained every letter from IRCC before I even had to ask. I never once felt like a file number.
Told us honestly on the first call that we didn't need a lawyer yet — saved us months of worry and a fee we didn't need to pay.
The only office that could talk about my refugee claim and my divorce in the same meeting, in Farsi.

items.question: How much does this cost?
items.answer: The first 30 minutes are always free, in English or Farsi. After that, we give you a flat fee up front wherever the type of case allows it — you'll know the number before you commit to anything.

items.question: How long does an immigration or family case take?
items.answer: It depends on the file — a straightforward sponsorship can move in months, a contested family matter or an appeal can take longer. On our first call we'll give you an honest, case-specific timeline, not a generic estimate.

items.question: What if my immigration status isn't fully in order?
items.answer: Come talk to us anyway. Everything you tell us is protected by solicitor–client privilege, and our job is to find the best path forward for your situation — not to judge how you got here.

items.question: Do I need to speak English well to work with you?
items.answer: No. Every stage of your case — the intake call, the strategy, the paperwork — can be done in Farsi or Dari as well as English.

items.question: What happens after I send an enquiry?
items.answer: A lawyer — not an intake form — reads it and replies within one business day. If you flag it as urgent, we move it up.

items.question: Can you handle both my immigration and family matters together?
items.answer: Yes — that overlap is exactly why the firm exists. One team, one file, no hand-off to a second lawyer at the moment it matters most.

contact.heading: Tell us what's happening.
contact.lede: Every enquiry is read by a lawyer, not an intake form. We reply within one business day — and if your matter is urgent, say so and we'll move it up.
